items.title: The boundary map of a square zero ideal extension of sheaves of rings is a derivation
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: Let O' to O be a surjection of sheaves of rings with square zero kernel I; the lemma shows that M = H^1(X, I) is a module over R = H^0(X, O) and that the boundary map R to M of the associated short exact sequence is a derivation (statement lines 5741-5752). The proof first observes that the conjugation map of O' into the sheaf of endomorphisms of I factors through O because the square of I vanishes, which gives both the O-module structure on I and hence the R-module structure on M (proof lines 5755-5758). Additivity being automatic, the author verifies the Leibniz rule explicitly: lift f and g locally along a covering, write the boundary classes as first Cech cocycles f_i - f_j and g_i - g_j with respect to that covering, and compute the cocycle of the product as the sum of the two terms, exactly as the Leibniz rule requires (proof lines 5759-5780). The claim is H2: the content is one algebraic observation plus a concrete cocycle computation, both written out in full.
